preamble.p:
on the basis of Articles 5, 12 paragraph 2, 13 paragraph 1, 16 paragraph 2, 19, 21 paragraph 2, 23, 39 paragraph 1, 40 and 45 of the Federal Act of 7 October 1983
SR 814.01 on the Protection of the Environment (the Act),

content.p: This Ordinance is intended to protect against harmful and disturbing noise.

blockList.listIntroduction: It regulates:

item.p: the limitation of exterior noise emissions caused by the operation of new and existing installations in accordance with Article 7 of the Act;

item.num:
b.
Amended by No I of the O of 25 Feb. 2026, in force since 1 April 2026 (AS 2026 114).
item.p: the designation of building zones and the amendment of land-use plans in areas exposed to noise;
the issuing of planning permission for buildings with rooms sensitive to noise and lying in areas exposed to noise;
the soundproofing against exterior and interior noise of new buildings with rooms sensitive to noise;
the soundproofing against exterior noise of existing buildings with rooms sensitive to noise;
the determination of the exposure to exterior noise and its rating based on exposure limit values.

blockList.listIntroduction: It does not regulate:

item.p: protection against noise originating from an industrial site as long as this only affects industrial buildings and dwellings within the site;
protection against infra- and ultrasound.

content.p:
…
Repealed by No I of the O of 12 April 2000, with effect from 1 May 2000 (AS 2000 1388).

Stationary installations are buildings, transport facilities, building facilities and other immobile equipment that generate exterior noise during operation. These include in particular roads, railway installations, aerodromes, industrial, commercial and agricultural installations, firing ranges and permanent military firing ranges and training grounds.
New stationary installations also include stationary installations and buildings whose use has been completely altered.

Emission limitation measures are technical, structural or functional modifications to installations, or measures to redirect, restrict or calm the flow of traffic, or structural measures along the emission path. The purpose of the measures is to prevent or reduce the generation or propagation of exterior noise.
Improvements are emission limitation measures for existing stationary installations.

Exposure limit values include impact thresholds, planning values and alarm values. These are set according to the noise characteristics, the time of day and the sensitivity to noise of the buildings and areas to be protected.

blockList.listIntroduction: Rooms sensitive to noise are:

item.p: rooms in dwellings with the exception of kitchens without dining facilities, washrooms and storerooms;
rooms in industrial buildings that are regularly occupied by persons for sustained periods of time, with the exception of those for farm animals and those with high levels of industrial noise.

content.p: Noise emitted from motorised vehicles, aircraft, water craft and railways must be reduced as far as possible by technical and operational means, and to the extent that this is economically acceptable.

Emission limitation measures are governed by the legislation on road traffic, civil aviation, inland navigation or the railways, provided the vehicle concerned is covered by one of these categories of legislation.
Emission limitation measures for other vehicles is governed by the provisions on mobile appliances and machines.

section.heading: Emission Limitation Measures for Mobile Appliances and Machines

blockList.listIntroduction: The emissions of exterior noise from mobile appliances and machines must be reduced to the extent that:

item.p: this is technically and operationally feasible and economically acceptable; and that
the well-being of the affected population is not seriously impaired.

content.p: The enforcement authorities shall order operational and structural measures, or those for proper maintenance.
Where it is not possible to avoid exposure to highly disturbing noise due to the operation of military equipment, machines and weapons, the enforcement authorities shall relax the requirements.
The emissions of appliances and machines that are used to operate a stationary installation are limited according to the provisions on stationary installations.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2006, in force since 1 Nov. 2006 (AS 2006 3693).

article.heading: Conformity assessment and marking of equipment and machines

content.p: Equipment and machines may be placed on the market only following a conformity assessment and the appropriate marking.

blockList.listIntroduction:
The Federal Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications (DETEC) shall specify:
Amended by No I of the O of 30 June 2010, in force since 1 Aug. 2010 (AS 2010 3223).

item.p: the types of equipment and machines subject to the conformity assessment and marking;
the requirements for preventive emission limitation measures and marking, taking into account internationally recognised standards;
the documents to be submitted for the purpose of the conformity assessment;
the test, measurement and calculation procedures;
the subsequent controls;
the recognition of foreign test results and labelling.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 29 Sept. 2023, in force since 1 Nov. 2023 (AS 2023 582).

content.p: The Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN) shall issue regulations covering structural and operational measures to control noise from building sites.

article.heading: Emission limitation measures for new stationary installations

blockList.listIntroduction: Noise emissions from new stationary installations shall be limited as directed by the enforcement authorities insofar as:

item.p: this is technically and operationally feasible and economically acceptable; and
the noise exposure level resulting from the installation alone does not exceed the planning values.

content.p:
The enforcement authorities shall relax the requirements in cases where compliance with the planning values would place a disproportionate burden on the installation and there is an overriding public interest, particularly regarding questions of spatial planning. The impact thresholds must not, however, be exceeded.
Amended by No I of the O of 16 June 1997, in force since 1 Aug. 1997 (AS 1997 1588).

In the case of new air-to-water heat pumps that are primarily used for space heating or for heating drinking water and whose noise emissions do not exceed the planning values, further emission limitation measures in accordance with paragraph 1 letter a shall only be taken if a limitation of emissions of at least 3 dB can be achieved with no more than one per cent of the investment costs of the system.
Inserted by No I of the O of 29 Sept. 2023, in force since 1 Nov. 2023 (AS 2023 582).

article.heading: Emission limitation measures for modified stationary installations

content.p:
Where a stationary installation that already exists when this Ordinance comes into force is modified, the noise emissions from the new or modified parts of the installation must be limited as directed by the enforcement authorities as far as this is technically and operationally feasible and economically acceptable.
Amended by No I of the O of 30 June 2010, in force since 1 Aug. 2010 (AS 2010 3223).
If the installation is significantly modified, the noise emissions from the installation as a whole must be limited at least to the extent that the impact thresholds are not exceeded.

Conversions, extensions and operational changes carried out by the person responsible for the installation constitute significant modifications to stationary installations if it is anticipated that the noise exposure level will rise perceptibly as a result either of the installation itself or of the increased demand on existing transport facilities. The rebuilding of an installation constitutes a significant modification irrespective of the circumstances.

If a new stationary installation is modified, Article 7 applies.
Amended by No I of the O of 16 June 1997, in force since 1 Aug. 1997 (AS 1997 1588).

blockList.listIntroduction: The operation of new or significantly modified stationary installations must not lead to a situation in which:

item.p: owing to the increased demand made on a transport facility, the impact thresholds are exceeded; or
owing to the increased demand made on a transport facility in need of remediation, the noise exposure level rises perceptibly.

content.p: If the requirements specified in Articles 7 paragraph 2 and 8 paragraph 2 or in Article 9 are not fulfilled by new or significantly modified public or licensed stationary installations, the enforcement authorities shall require the owners of existing buildings exposed to noise to soundproof the windows of rooms sensitive to noise in accordance with Annex 1.
With the approval of the enforcement authorities, building owners may carry out other structural soundproofing measures provided these reduce the noise within the rooms to the same extent.

blockList.listIntroduction: Soundproofing measures need not be taken if:

item.p: no perceptible reduction of the noise level in the building is to be expected;
they conflict with the overriding interest of preserving local character or monuments;

the building is due to be demolished within three years of putting the new or modified installation into service, or the rooms concerned will be converted to purposes not sensitive to noise within this period.

content.p: The person responsible for the new or significantly modified installation bears the costs of limiting the emission it causes.

blockList.listIntroduction: If the building owner is required to take soundproofing measures according to Article 10 paragraph 1, the person responsible for the installation also bears the customary local costs proven to be due for:

item.p: engineering and supervision of works;
soundproofing of the windows in accordance with Annex 1 and the resulting necessary adaptations;
the financing if the person responsible has failed to contribute despite being requested to do so by the building owner;
any fees due.

content.p: If the building owner is required to take soundproofing measures according to Article 10 paragraph 2, the person responsible for the installation bears the customary local costs proven to be due insofar as these do not exceed those under paragraph 2. The building owner bears the remaining costs.

Where the need for emission limitation measures or soundproofing measures arises as a result of noise from several installations, the costs are divided among the installations in proportion to their contribution to the noise exposure level.
The building owner bears the costs for maintenance and renewal of the soundproofing measures.

The enforcement authorities shall inspect the new or modified installation within one year of its being put into service to check whether the emission limitation and soundproofing measures ordered have been taken. In the event of any doubt, they carry out tests to assess the effectiveness of the measures.

In the case of stationary installations that contribute significantly to the impact thresholds being exceeded, the enforcement authorities shall order the necessary improvement measures, after hearing the persons responsible for the installations.

blockList.listIntroduction: The installations shall be improved to the extent that:

item.p: is technically and operationally feasible and economically acceptable; and
the impact thresholds are no longer exceeded.

content.p: Unless there are overriding interests, the enforcement authorities give priority to measures which prevent or reduce noise generation in preference to those which simply prevent or reduce noise propagation.

blockList.listIntroduction: Improvements need not be carried out if:

item.p: the impact thresholds are exceeded only in building zones that have not yet been developed;

due to the cantonal building and planning legislation, planning, design or structural measures taken at the site exposed to the noise will satisfy the impact thresholds before the time limit specified in Article 17.

article.heading: Relaxation of the requirements for improvements

blockList.listIntroduction: The enforcement authorities shall relax the requirements in cases where:

item.p: improvements would result in unreasonable operational limitations or costs;

overriding interests, namely those of the preservation of local character, nature and landscape protection, traffic and operational safety, or national security, conflict with the improvement objective.

content.p: Unlicensed private installations must not, however, exceed the alarm values.

If, as a result of relaxing the requirements, the alarm values for public or licensed stationary installations cannot be complied with, the enforcement authorities shall require the owners of existing buildings exposed to noise to soundproof the windows of rooms sensitive to noise in accordance with Annex 1.
With the approval of the enforcement authorities, building owners may take other soundproofing measures in the building provided these reduce the noise within the rooms to the same extent.

blockList.listIntroduction: Soundproofing measures need not be taken if:

item.p: no perceptible reduction of noise in the building is to be expected;
they conflict with the overriding interest of preserving local character or monuments;
the building is due to be demolished within three years of the soundproofing measures being ordered, or the rooms will be converted to purposes not sensitive to noise within this period.

content.p: The person responsible for the installation bears the costs of its improvement.

The person responsible for a public or licensed installation also bears the costs of soundproofing measures for existing buildings under Article 11, unless an exemption has been granted under Article 20 paragraph 2 of the Act.

Where improvements or soundproofing measures are required as a result of noise from several installations, the costs are divided among the installations in proportion to their contribution to the noise exposure level.
The building owner bears the costs of maintenance and renewal of the soundproofing measures.
The enforcement authorities set the time limits for implementing improvements and soundproofing measures according to their urgency.

blockList.listIntroduction: In assessing urgency, the following factors are decisive:

item.p: the extent to which the impact thresholds are exceeded;
the number of persons affected by the noise;
the cost-benefit relationship.

content.p: The improvements and soundproofing measures must be completed within 15 years of this Ordinance coming into force.

blockList.listIntroduction: The time limit (para. 3) for improvements and soundproofing measures on roads are extended:

item.p: for national roads until 31 March 2015;

for trunk roads according to Article 12 of the Federal Act of 22 March 1985
SR 725.116.2 on the Application of the Earmarked Mineral Oil Tax (MinOA), and for other roads until 31 March 2018
Inserted by No I of the O of 1 Sept. 2004, in force since 1 Oct. 2004 (AS 2004 4167). .

content.p:
The time limits specified in the Federal Act of 24 March 2000
SR 742.144 on Railways Noise Abatement apply to the completion of improvements and soundproofing measures on railway installations.
Inserted by No I of the O of 1 Sept. 2004, in force since 1 Oct. 2004 (AS 2004 4167).

blockList.listIntroduction: The improvements and soundproofing measures must be completed:

item.p: at military aerodromes by 31 July 2020;
at civil aerodromes that are used by heavy aircraft by 31 May 2016;

at military firing ranges and training grounds: by 31 July 2025.
Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2006 (AS 2006 3693). Amended by No I of the O of 30 June 2010, in force since 1 Aug. 2010 (AS 2010 3223).

content.p: Within one year of completion, the enforcement authorities shall inspect the improvements and soundproofing measures to check compliance with the measures ordered. In case of doubt, they carry out tests to assess the effectiveness of the measures.

authorialNote.p: Repealed by No I of the O of 1 Sept. 2004, with effect from 1 Oct. 2004 (AS 2004 4167).
Amended by No I 14 of the O of 7 Nov. 2007 on the New System of Fiscal Equalisation and Division of Tasks between the Confederation and the Cantons, in force since 1 Jan. 2008 (AS 2007 5823).

The FOEN

This amendment has been made throughout the text. shall enquire regularly of the enforcement authorities as to the status of the improvements and the noise protection measures, in particular concerning roads, railway installations, aerodromes, shooting ranges and military shooting ranges and training areas.

blockList.listIntroduction: For roads, the enforcement authorities must provide the following documents in particular by 31 March each year:
a summary of:

item.p: the roads or sections of road requiring improvements,
the time frame within which these roads and sections of road will be improved,
the total costs of these improvements and noise protection measures, and
the number of persons exposed to noise levels above the impact thresholds and alarm values;

blockList.listIntroduction: a report on:

item.p: the improvements made to roads and sections of road, and the soundproofing measures implemented in the previous year, and
the effectiveness and the costs of these improvements and noise protection measures.

content.p: For national roads, it shall obtain the information under Paragraph 2 from the Federal Roads Office. For trunk roads and other roads it shall obtain this information from the cantons. The information must be submitted in accordance with the requirements of the FOEN.

The FOEN shall assess the information in particular in relation to the progress made with improvements and the costs and effectiveness of the measures. It shall inform the enforcement authorities of the results and publishes them.

article.heading: Inadequate fulfilment and misuse of subsidies

blockList.listIntroduction: The FOEN shall withhold all or part of the instalment payments during the programme if the canton:

item.p: fails to fulfil its reporting duty (Art. 26 para. 1);
fails to meet its obligations to a substantial extent through its own fault.

content.p: If on conclusion of the programme it emerges that the canton has failed to meet its obligations, the competent Federal Office shall require the canton to rectify the situation; it shall set the Canton an appropriate deadline for doing so.
If installations for which subsidies have been made are used for a purpose other than that intended, the FOEN may require the canton to cease or make good the misuse within a reasonable period.

If the defects are not rectified or the misuse does not stop or is not remedied, the subsidies may be reclaimed in accordance with Articles 28 and 29 of the Subsidies Act of 5 October 1990
SR 616.1 .

chapter.heading: Requirements for Building Zones and Planning Permission in Areas exposed to Noise

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 25 Feb. 2026, with effect from 1 April 2026 (AS 2026 114).

article.heading: Designation of building zones and amendments to land-use plans in areas exposed to noise

content.p: The relevant exposure limit values can be met through planning, design or construction measures.

Open spaces referred to in Article 24 paragraph 3 letter b of the Act must be of a reasonable size and accessible on foot without any obstacles. They shall feature a design and infrastructure geared towards recreation.

The measures referred to in Article 24 paragraph 3 letter c of the Act must be determined according to the relevant level. From an acoustic point of view, they shall contribute to an appropriate quality of life by limiting noise emissions or otherwise reducing any impairment of well-being.

authorialNote.p: Repealed by No I of the O of 25 Feb. 2026, with effect from 1 April 2026 (AS 2026 114).

article.heading: Planning permission in areas subject to noise

blockList.listIntroduction: If the impact thresholds are exceeded, new buildings and significant modifications to buildings with rooms sensitive to noise may only be authorised if the values can be complied with:

item.p: by locating the rooms sensitive to noise on the side of the building away from the source of the noise; or

by structural or design measures which shield the building against noise.
Amended by No I of the O of 16 June 1997, in force since 1 Aug. 1997 (AS 1997 1588).

content.p:
Controlled domestic ventilation and cooling systems must be state of the art.
Inserted by No I of the O of 25 Feb. 2026, in force since 1 April 2026 (AS 2026 114).

If the requirements of Article 22 paragraph 2 letter a of the Act cannot be met in relation to aircraft noise or where no more than ten per cent of the residential units in large housing developments are affected, a building permit may be granted by way of exception if there is an overriding interest in the construction of the building and the cantonal authority gives its consent.
Amended by No I of the O of 25 Feb. 2026, in force since 1 April 2026 (AS 2026 114).
The landowners bear the costs of the measures.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 28 Nov. 2014 (AS 2014 4501). Repealed by No I of the O of 25 Feb. 2026, with effect from 1 April 2026 (AS 2026 114).

content.p:
The project owner of a new building shall ensure that the soundproofing of the external building elements and partitions of rooms sensitive to noise, and of the stairs and building facilities complies with recognised codes of building practice. These are in particular, for noise from civil aerodromes that are used by heavy aircraft, the stricter requirements, and for noise from other stationary installations, the minimum requirements, of SIA Standard No 181 of the Swiss Society of Engineers and Architects.
Sentence amended by No I of the O of 12 April 2000, in force since 1 May 2000 (AS 2000 1388).

If the ambient limit values are exceeded but the requirements of Article paragraph 22 for granting a building permit are met, the enforcement authorities shall impose stricter requirements for the soundproofing of the external building elements appropriately. The costs associated with these stricter requirements shall generally be considered reasonable if they do not exceed one per cent of the building costs.
Amended by No I of the O of 25 Feb. 2026, in force since 1 April 2026 (AS 2026 114).

The requirements also apply to the external building elements, partitions, stairways and building facilities that are converted, replaced or newly installed. On request, the enforcement authorities grant relief if compliance with the requirements would involve unreasonable cost.

article.heading: External building elements, partitions and building facilities

content.p: External building elements form the external boundary of a room (e.g. windows, external doors, external walls, roofs).
Partitions (e.g. internal walls, ceilings, doors) serve to separate individual units, such as dwellings, within the building.
Building facilities are fixed installations such as heating, ventilation, supply and disposal systems, lifts and washing machines.

blockList.listIntroduction: The project owner must specify in the application:

item.num:
a.
Amended by No I of the O of 25 Feb. 2026, in force since 1 April 2026 (AS 2026 114).
item.p: the exterior noise pollution and the measures assessed in accordance with Article 31 paragraph 1 in the event that the ambient limit values have been exceeded;
the use to which the rooms are put;
the external building elements and partitions of rooms sensitive to noise.

content.p: For building projects in areas in which the impact thresholds are exceeded, the enforcement authorities may demand details of the soundproofing of the external building elements.

After building works are completed, the enforcement authorities shall make random checks to verify whether the soundproofing measures comply with the requirements. In the event of any doubt, they must carry out a more detailed inspection.

chapter.heading:
Investigation, Assessment and Control of Exposure to Exterior Noise due to Stationary Installations

content.p: The enforcement authorities shall investigate the exposure to exterior noise due to stationary installations, or order its investigation if they have grounds to believe that the relevant exposure limit values are being exceeded or that this is to be expected.

blockList.listIntroduction: They shall take account of increases and reductions in noise exposure levels that are to be expected due to:

item.p: the construction, alteration or improvement of stationary installations, in particular if the projects in question have already been approved or made available for public inspection at the time of the investigation; and
the construction, alteration or demolition of other structures if the projects have been made available for public inspection at the time of the investigation.

content.p:
In the case of roads, railway installations, aerodromes and military firing ranges and training grounds, the enforcement authorities shall record in specific registers (noise pollution registers) the noise exposure levels measured in accordance with Article 36.
Amended by No I of the O of 30 June 2010, in force since 1 Aug. 2010 (AS 2010 3223).

blockList.listIntroduction: The noise pollution registers specify:

item.p: the noise pollution measured;
the calculation procedure used;
the input data for the calculation;
the classification of the areas exposed to noise in the land use plan;
the sensitivity levels applicable;
the installations and their owners;
the number of persons who are affected by noise exposure levels above the applicable exposure limit values.

content.p: The enforcement authorities are responsible for the supervision and revision of the registers.
On request, they submit the noise pollution registers to the FOEN. The Office may issue recommendations on the standardised recording and presentation of the data.
The Federal Office for Civil Aviation is responsible for measurement of noise exposure levels produced by Basel Mulhouse Airport on Swiss territory.

Any person may have access to the noise pollution register provided that confidentiality with respect to manufacturing and business secrets is ensured, and no conflict with other interests that override exists.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 12 April 2000 (AS 2000 1388). Amended by No I of the O of 1 Sept. 2004, in force since 1 Oct. 2004 (AS 2004 4167).

article.heading: Determination and control of noise exposure levels

content.p: The enforcement authorities state the permitted noise exposure level in their decision on the construction, alteration or improvement of an installation.

If it is established or anticipated that the noise exposure levels due to an installation will deviate significantly and permanently from those quoted in the decision, the enforcement authorities shall take the necessary measures.
The FOEN may issue recommendations on the standardised recording and presentation of the noise exposure levels in these decisions.

Noise exposure levels are determined in the form of a rating sound level, Lr, or a maximum sound level, Lmax, on the basis of calculations or measurements.
Amended by No I of the O of 1 Sept. 2004, in force since 1 Oct. 2004 (AS 2004 4167 4313).

Noise exposure levels due to aircraft shall principally be determined by calculation. The calculations are carried out using recognised state-of-the-art methods. The FOEN shall recommend suitable calculation procedures.
Inserted by No I of the O of 12 April 2000, in force since 1 May 2000 (AS 2000 1388).

The requirements for calculation procedures and measuring instruments are given in Annex 2.
Originally para. 2.

For buildings, noise exposure levels shall be determined at the centre of open windows in rooms sensitive to noise. Noise exposure levels due to aircraft may also be determined in the vicinity of the building.
The correction of 7 May 2019 concerns the French text only (AS 2019 1337).
In the non-developed sector of zones with higher noise abatement requirements, noise exposure levels shall be measured 1.5 m above the ground.
In building zones that have not yet been developed, noise exposure levels shall be measured at points where the building and planning legislation allows the building of rooms sensitive to noise.

For outdoor areas intended for private use, noise levels are measured 1.5 metres above the ground in the outdoor area.
Inserted by No I of the O of 25 Feb. 2026, in force since 1 April 2026 (AS 2026 114).
The enforcement authorities shall rate the exposure to exterior noise due to stationary installations on the basis of the exposure limit values specified in Annexes 3 ff.

The exposure limit value, it is also considered exceeded if it is less than the sum of the levels of exposure to similar types of noise generated by several installations. This does not apply to the planning values for new stationary installations (Art. 7 para. 1).

In the absence of exposure limit values, the enforcement authorities shall rate the noise exposure levels in accordance with Article 15 of the Act. They shall also take account of Articles 19 and 23 of the Act.

article.heading: Validity of the exposure limit values

content.p: The exposure limit values apply to buildings with rooms sensitive to noise.

blockList.listIntroduction: They also apply:

item.p: in yet undeveloped building zones in areas where the construction of buildings with rooms sensitive to noise is allowed under the building and planning legislation;
in the non-developed areas of zones with higher noise abatement requirements.

content.p:
The ambient limit values also apply if a building permit is granted to the entire area of the privately used outdoor space specified in Article 22 paragraph 2 letter a number 3 of the Act.
Inserted by No I of the O of 25 Feb. 2026, in force since 1 April 2026 (AS 2026 114).
For areas and buildings in which, as a rule, people are present either only during the day or only at night, no exposure limit values apply at night or during the day.

article.heading: Special exposure limit values for rooms in industrial buildings

content.p: For rooms in industrial buildings (Art. 2 para. 6 let. b) lying in areas of sensitivity levels I, II or III, the planning and impact thresholds shall be increased by 5 dB(A).
Paragraph 1 does not apply to rooms in schools, institutions and homes. It applies to hotels and guesthouses only if these can be adequately ventilated when the windows are closed.

blockList.listIntroduction:
In land use zones according to Articles 14 ff. of the Spatial Planning Act of 22 June 1979
SR 700 , the following sensitivity levels apply:

item.p: sensitivity level I in zones with higher noise abatement requirements, notably in leisure zones;
sensitivity level II in zones in which operations that emit noise are not permitted, notably in residential zones and zones for public buildings and installations;
sensitivity level III in zones in which operations emitting a certain level of noise are permitted, notably in residential and industrial zones (mixed zones) and agricultural zones;
sensitivity level IV in zones in which operations emitting a high level of noise are permitted, notably in industrial zones.

content.p: Parts of land use zones rated as sensitivity levels I or II may be assigned the next higher level if they are already exposed to noise.
The cantons shall ensure that sensitivity levels are assigned to the land use zones in the building regulations or land use plans of the communes.

The sensitivity levels are assigned at the time of designation or modification of the land use zones, or at the time of modification of the building regulations.
Amended by No IV 31 of the O of 22 Aug. 2007 on the Formal Revision of Federal Legislation, in force since 1 Jan. 2008 (AS 2007 4477).
Prior to assignment, the cantons shall determine the sensitivity levels on a case by case basis in accordance with Article 43.

article.heading:
Responsibilities of the Confederation and the cantons
Inserted by Annex 2 No 9 of the O of 21 May 2008 on Geoinformation, in force since 1 July 2008 (AS 2008 2809).

content.p: The cantons shall enforce this Ordinance unless it delegates enforcement to the Confederation.

If the federal authorities apply other federal laws or international treaties or decisions that relate to the subject matter of this Ordinance, they shall also enforce this Ordinance. The cooperation of the FOEN and the cantons is governed by Article 41 paragraphs 2 and 4 of the Act; statutory duties of secrecy are reserved.

blockList.listIntroduction: The following authorities are responsible for enforcing the provisions governing emission limitation measures (Art. 4, 7–9 and 12), improvements (Art. 13, 14, 16–18 and 20) and the determination and control of noise exposure levels (Art. 36, 37, 37a and 40):
for railway installations:

item.p:
DETEC, where the provisions relate to major railway projects under the Annex to the Railways Act of 20 December 1957
SR 742.101 and are implemented by means of a planning approval procedure,
in other cases, the Federal Office of Transport;

blockList.listIntroduction: for civil aerodromes:

item.p:
DETEC, where the provisions relate to buildings and installations under Article 37 of the Air Navigation Act of 21 December 1948
SR 748.0 that are used for operation of an aerodrome and are implemented by means of a planning approval procedure,
in other cases, the Federal Office of Civil Aviation;

blockList.listIntroduction: for national roads:

item.p: DETEC, where the provisions are implemented by means of a planning approval procedure,
in other cases the Federal Roads Office;
for national defence installations: the Federal Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport;

blockList.listIntroduction: for electrical installations:

item.p:
the Swiss Federal Office of Energy in cases where the Federal Inspectorate for Heavy Current Installations (ESTI) has been unable to deal with objections from or resolve disputes with the Federal authorities concerned, in accordance with Article 16 paragraph 2 letter b of the Electricity Act of 24 June 1902
SR 734.0 ,
in other cases the ESTI;

for cable railway installations according to Article 2 of the Cable Railways Act of 23 June 2006
SR 743.01 : the Federal Office of Transport
Amended by No I of the O of 30 June 2010, in force since 1 Aug. 2010 (AS 2010 3223). .

content.p: In cases where the responsibility for ordering emission limitation measures and improvements lies with the federal authorities, but that for noise protection lies with the cantonal authorities, the two authorities shall coordinate the necessary measures.

For national roads, DETEC is also responsible for enforcing the provisions governing soundproofing measures (Art. 10 and 15). It coordinates the enforcement of these provisions with the soundproofing measures that are arranged by the cantons.
Inserted by No I of the O of 30 June 2010, in force since 1 Aug. 2010 (AS 2010 3223).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 30 June 2010, in force since 1 Aug. 2010 (AS 2010 3223).

content.p: The FOEN shall conduct a national survey of noise pollution. It shall publish a geo-referenced presentation of the noise pollution in particular for road, railway and aircraft noise and for noise from military firing ranges and training grounds. It shall updates this presentation at least every five years.

authorialNote.p: Amended by Annex 2 No 9 of the O of 21 May 2008 on Geoinformation, in force since 1 July 2008 (AS 2008 2809).

content.p:
The FOEN shall provide specifications for the minimal geodata models and presentation models for official geodata under this Ordinance, for which it is designated as the federal specialist authority in Annex 1 to the Geoinformation Ordinance of 21 May 2008
SR 510.620 .

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2006, in force since 1 Nov. 2006 (AS 2006 3693).

content.p: Stationary installations are deemed to be new stationary installations if the decision authorising the start of building work has not yet taken full legal effect when this Ordinance comes into force.
For stationary installations that are to be modified, Articles 8-12 apply only if the decision authorising the modification has not yet taken full legal effect when this Ordinance comes into force.
Buildings are deemed to be new buildings if planning permission has not yet taken full legal effect when this Ordinance comes into force.
For buildings that must be modified, Articles 31 and 32 paragraph 3 apply only if planning permission has not yet taken full legal effect when this Ordinance comes into force.

level.heading: Requirements for the Calculation Procedures and Measuring Instruments

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 The procedures used to calculate noise exposure levels must take account of:

item.p: the emissions from the noise source of the installation;
the distance between the exposure point and the noise source of the installation or the flight paths (attenuation due to propagation and dissipation);
the influence of the ground on the propagation of the noise (ground effects);
the influence of buildings and natural obstacles on the propagation of the noise (attenuation due to obstacles and reflection).

content.p: 2 The FOEN (FOEN) recommends suitable state-of-the-art calculation procedures to the enforcement authorities.

The requirements of the Measuring Instruments Ordinance of 15 February 2006
SR 941.210 and the corresponding implementing provisions of the Federal Justice and Police Department apply to the instruments used to measure noise exposure levels.

level.heading: Exposure Limit Values for Road Traffic Noise

content.p: The exposure limit values specified in Number 2 apply to road traffic noise. This includes noise on roads from motor vehicles (motor vehicle noise) and railways (railway noise).

level.heading: Determination of the Rating Sound Level

content.p: 1 The rating sound level Lr for road traffic noise is determined from the partial rating sound levels for motor vehicle noise (Lr1) and railway noise (Lr2) as follows:
2 The partial rating sound level Lr1 is the sum of the equivalent continuous A‑weighted sound level Leq,m resulting from motor vehicles, and the level correction K1:
Lr1 = Leq,m + K1
3 The partial rating sound level Lr2 is the sum of the equivalent continuous A‑weighted sound level Leq,b resulting from the railways, and the level correction K2:
Lr2 = Leq,b + K2
4 The partial rating sound levels Lr1 and Lr2 are determined for average day and night traffic flows assuming a dry road surface.
1 The average day and night traffic is defined as the annual average of the hourly traffic between 06 and 22 hours and between 22 and 06 hours.
2 The hourly motor vehicle traffic during the day (Nt) and at night (Nn) are each divided into two partial traffic flows, Nt1 and Nt2, and Nn1 and Nn2, respectively.
3 The partial traffic flows Nt1 and Nn1 for motor vehicle traffic include private cars, delivery vehicles, minibuses, motorcycles and trolley buses.
4 The partial traffic flows Nt2 and Nn2 for motor vehicle traffic comprise lorries, articulated lorries, coaches, motorcycles and tractors.
5 Railway traffic comprises all scheduled and non-scheduled trains, including service journeys.

level.heading: Determination of Average Day and Night Motor Vehicle Traffic

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 The average day and night traffic (Nt, Nn) and the partial traffic flows (Nt1, Nt2, Nn1, Nn2) are determined:

item.p: from traffic surveys for existing roads;
from forecasts of traffic volume for roads which are to be built or modified.

content.p: 2 Where insufficient data is available from traffic surveys, or no detailed forecasts exist, the traffic flows Nt, Nn, Nt1, Nt2, Nn1 and Nn2 are calculated from the average daily traffic (ADT; vehicles per 24 h) as follows:
Nt = 0.058 ⋅ ADT Nn = 0.009 ⋅ ADT
3 The ADT is determined according to the recognised principles of traffic planning and traffic technology.

level.heading: Determination of the Average Day and Night Traffic for Railways

blockList.listIntroduction: The average day and night traffic for railways is determined:

item.p: from the timetable and traffic data for existing railway installations;
from traffic volume forecasts for railway installations which are to be built or modified.

content.p: 1 At civil aerodromes used by heavy aircraft, the rating sound level Lr of total traffic is determined based on the relevant aircraft traffic, whereby separate calculations are made for daytime (06-22 hours), and for the first (22-23 hours), second (23-24 hours) and last (05-06 hours) night hours.

level.heading: Exposure Limit Values for Industrial and Commercial Noise

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 The exposure limit values specified in Number 2 apply to noise:

item.p: from industrial, commercial and agricultural installations;
from goods handling in industrial, commercial and agricultural installations and at railway stations, aerodromes, etc.;
from traffic within the perimeter of industrial and commercial installations and farmyards;
from multi-storey car parks and from larger off-road car parks;
from heating, ventilation and air-conditioning installations.

content.p: 2 Energy, waste processing and transport installations, aerial cableways and cable railways, ski lifts and racing tracks that are used regularly for sustained periods of time are considered equivalent to industrial and commercial installations.

level.heading: Determination of the Rating Sound Level

content.p: 1 The rating sound level Lr for industrial, commercial and similar types of noise is determined from the partial rating sound levels Lr,i for each noise phase as follows, whereby separate calculations are made for daytime (07 to 19 hours) and night-time (19 to 07 hours):
2 The partial rating sound level Lr,i is determined for the average daily duration of the noise phase i as follows:
Lr,i = Leq,i + K1,i + K2,i + K3,i + 10 x log (ti/to)
where:
Leq,i is the equivalent continuous A-weighted sound level during the noise phase i;
K1,i is the level correction for the noise phase i;
K2,i is the level correction for the noise phase i;
K3,i is the level correction for the noise phase i;
ti is the average daily duration of the noise phase i in minutes;
to = 720 minutes.
3 Noise phases are time periods in which the exposure point is subject to uniform noise with respect to sound level, frequency and pulse content.

level.heading: Average Daily Duration of Noise Phases

content.p: 1 The average daily duration (ti) of the noise phase i is calculated from its annual duration (Ti) and the annual number of working days (B) as follows:
ti = Ti/B
2 For new or modified installations, the average daily duration of the noise phase i is determined from operational forecasts.

level.heading: Exposure Limit Values for Noise at Military Aerodromes

content.p: 1 The exposure limit values specified in Number 2 apply to traffic noise from military aerodromes.
2 Civil regional airports and airfields used for military purposes also count as military aerodromes.
3 Helicopters are considered equivalent to propeller aircraft.

4 Noise from repair workshops, maintenance workshops and similar operations at military aerodromes is considered equivalent to the noise from industrial and commercial installations (Annex 6 Number 1).

level.heading: Exposure Limit Values expressed as Lr
Exposure Limit Values expressed as Lrz

content.p: In addition to the exposure limit values expressed as Lr, the exposure limit values specified in Annex 5 and expressed as Lr, referred to below as Lrz, also apply to the noise from civilian traffic at military airfields.

level.heading: Determination of the Rating Sound Level

content.p: 1 The rating sound level Lr for noise from military aerodromes is calculated from the rating sound levels Lrm for military aircraft noise and Lrz for civil aircraft noise, as follows:
2 The rating sound level Lrz is determined in the same way as the corresponding Lr for civil aerodromes specified in Annex 5 Numbers 3 and 4.
3 The rating sound level Lrm is determined from the partial rating sound levels Lrj, for noise from jet aircraft, and Lrp, for noise from propeller aircraft, as follows:
4 The partial rating sound level Lrj is the sum of the equivalent continuous A-weighted sound level Leqj arising from the operation of jet aircraft, and the level corrections K0 and K1:
Lrj = Leqj + K0 + K1
5 The partial rating sound level Lrp is the sum of the equivalent continuous A-weighted sound level Leqp arising from the operation of propeller aircraft, and the level corrections K0 and K2:
Lrp = Leqp + K0 + K2

6 The equivalent continuous sound levels Leqj and Leqp are calculated for the average number of hourly flight movements for a day with an average level of traffic, whereby flight movements of jet aircraft and propeller aircraft are counted separately (number of flight movements nj and np).
7 Flight movements are all takeoffs and landings of jet and propeller aircraft. Go-arounds count as two flight movements.

level.heading: Numbers of Flight Movements nj and np for Military Aerodromes

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 For existing military aerodromes, the number of flight movements nj and np are determined as follows:

item.p: the six months of the operating year with the greatest amount of traffic are identified, whereby flight movements of jet aircraft and propeller aircraft are counted separately;
for these six months, the number of flight movements of jet aircraft Mj and propeller aircraft Mp are determined;
the numbers of flight movements nj and np are calculated from Mj and Mp by averaging them over 130 days and twelve daytime hours:

content.p: 2 For military aerodromes that are to be built or modified, the numbers of flight movements nj and np are determined from forecasts of traffic volume.
1 The level correction K0 is equal to -8.
2 The level correction K1 is calculated from the annual number of flight movements of jet aircraft Nj as follows:
K1 = 0 for Nj < 15 000
K1 = 10 x log (Nj/15 000) for Nj ≥ 15 000
3 The level correction K2 is calculated from the annual number of flight movements of propeller aircraft Np as follows:
K2 = 0 for Np < 15 000
K2 = 10 x log (Np/15 000) for Np ≥ 15 000

level.heading: Exposure Limit Values for Noise from Military Firing Ranges and Training Grounds

content.p: 1 The exposure limit values specified in Number 2 apply to the firing noise on military firing ranges and training grounds.

2 In addition to the exposure limit values specified in Number 2, the exposure limit values specified in Annex 7 apply to the noise from civil firing on military firing ranges and training grounds, with the exception of firing by the police and border guards.

3 Noise from repair workshops, maintenance workshops and similar operations and noise from traffic on military firing ranges and training grounds is considered equivalent to the noise from industrial and commercial installations (Annex 6 Number 1).
4 Noise from helicopters on military firing ranges and training grounds is considered equivalent to the noise from heliports (Annex 5 Numbers 23 and 5).

level.heading: Determination of the Rating Sound Level
